title: The Hinge of the Jaw

beats.text: Elias stood before the heavy oak door, the iron padlock cold against his palm. From the darkness behind the wood, his grandmother’s voice drifted up, smelling of dried lavender.
beats.image_prompt: monochrome shot of a heavy wooden cellar door with a large iron padlock in a dark hallway

beats.text: Stay for tea, Elias, she murmured, the same lilt that had tucked him in for twenty years, despite her burial in the churchyard last spring.
beats.image_prompt: monochrome dark cellar stairs disappearing into pitch black shadow

beats.text: He fumbled with the rusted key, needing to see her face one last time to soothe the ache in his chest. The bolt slid back with a heavy, final groan.
beats.image_prompt: close up of a hand inserting a rusty key into an old lock monochrome

beats.text: He swung the door wide to find the stone room perfectly, hauntingly empty, his flashlight cutting through nothing but settling dust and cold air.
beats.image_prompt: monochrome wide shot of an empty stone basement room with dust motes

beats.text: Then, the voice spoke again, not from the shadows, but from the hinge of his own jaw. Stay for tea, he whispered, his own hands moving to lock himself inside.
beats.image_prompt: monochrome close up of a man's face in shadow locking a door from the inside

disclosure: An original fictional horror story. Visuals are illustrative.
